correctness.rationale: PASS: The forbidden-third-edge predicate is equivalent to B being an induced disjoint union of stars; rook-row and rook-column neighbor cliques force components to be 2-edge corners or single horizontal/vertical edges. Distinct components must have disjoint row and column indices, giving exact resource constraints R=2a+b+2c<=m, C=2a+2b+c<=n. Counting unordered row and column groups, matching like types and four corner-center choices produces the stated factorial coefficient with denominator 2^(b+c)a!b!c! and no double-counting. The resource bounds show t<=min(m,n), parity loss on odd squares, and every equality case by b,c constraints. An independent edge-pair forbidden-third-edge exhaustive implementation recovered all coefficients and maximum-counts for 2x2,2x3,2x4,3x3,3x4,4x4; no claim is based on extending finite data.

value.rationale: PASS: K_m Cartesian K_n is the canonical two-factor Hamming/rook graph. A complete all-size enumerating polynomial, precise parity obstruction on odd-square boards and all labeled maximizing configurations are natural structural strengthening of existing edge-open-packing bounds. They are potentially useful as exact benchmarks for product graph packing and induced-star constraints.

final_claim: For m,n>=2, every edge-open-packing on K_m Cartesian K_n decomposes uniquely into disjoint row-and-column-support corners (two edges), horizontal or vertical single edges. Its complete polynomial has coefficients m!n!/[2^(b+c)a!b!c!(m-2a-b-2c)!(n-2a-2b-c)!] for admissible triples (a,b,c), maximum min(m,n)-1 if m=n odd and min(m,n) otherwise, with exact labeled counts and configurations of all maxima.
limitations: Simple graphs m,n>=2, labeled boards and original third-edge packing predicate; finite original-definition census is limited to displayed six boards.
residual_risks: Unindexed rook/induced-star-forest enumeration, possibly the earlier 2022 paper or a supplement, may already imply the polynomial.
Only two-factor Cartesian products of complete graphs are covered, not arbitrary Hamming graphs or other product classes.
